clue.text: Tame doc meditates after major surgery

indicators.note: something after major surgery has been cut up and put back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who meditates has been subdued after undergoing a big operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after major surgery' looks like a time phrase, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of DOC MEDITATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an animal brought under human control and kept as a pet or livestock.

clue.text: Son affected with guilt showing personal talent

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy troubled by guilt reveals an individual gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' tells you to rearrange SON and GUILT together. A long suit is originally a card game term: a long run of cards in one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from card play: a strong suit you hold many cards in becomes a figure for something you are especially good at.

clue.text: King Edward who wrote nonsense

definitions.meaning: King ... is the title king of Shakespeare's tragedy
Edward ... was the Victorian author of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: A reference to a royal Edward who was famous for nonsense writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a King Edward, but it is two separate definitions: Shakespeare's king, and the nonsense poet Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: One surname serves both a Shakespearean monarch and the Victorian writer of limericks and nonsense poems.

clue.text: Sportsperson quietly lying on bed?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
a layer is something lying on a bed, as a stratum lies on a bed of rock; the question mark flags the playful definition

explanation.surface: An athlete is quietly lying in bed, resting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying on bed' is a cryptic description of a layer, which sits on top of a bed or base.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who takes part in a game or sport is called a participant of that kind.

clue.text: Pleaded with troublemaker, peer needing to be heard

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil, a troublemaker

indicators.note: to be heard means the word for peer is spoken, and its sound spelt differently

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: Someone begged a mischief-maker while a nobleman wanted a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD said out loud gives the ending LORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean begged someone earnestly and desperately for something.

clue.text: Appropriate to grasp start of news report

indicators.note: to grasp means the first word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to bag something is to appropriate or take it for yourself

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter of news

explanation.surface: It is fitting to take hold of the opening of a news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a news report, but it means a loud noise, as of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a sharp explosive sound, like a gunshot, which is a sudden loud noise.

clue.text: Love region — there's something in the atmosphere

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: Romance in an area: there is something in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas forms a protective layer high in the air, shielding the earth from ultraviolet radiation.

clue.text: Recline when consuming honey drink: fizzy one?

indicators.note: when consuming means the first word swallows the other piece inside it

parts.note: to lie is to recline
mead is an alcoholic drink made from fermented honey

explanation.surface: Lying back while sipping a honey drink, wondering if it is sparkling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'fizzy one?' leans back on the word 'drink' in the wordplay: a fizzy drink. 'Recline' is the verb, not a resting position.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime-flavoured soft drink, often carbonated, is an example of a sparkling beverage.

clue.text: The subject of his study rather creepy?

definitions.text: The subject of his study rather creepy?

parts.words: The subject of his study rather creepy?
parts.note: creepy here means creepy-crawly: the scientist studies insects, things that creep

explanation.surface: Someone's field of research seems rather sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creepy' seems to mean unsettling, but it means literally creeping: insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: an insect scientist studies creatures that crawl, hence a creepy subject.

clue.text: Showing keenness ahead of time, starts to get excited inside

indicators.note: inside means those first letters go within the other piece

parts.note: early means ahead of time

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letters of get and excited

explanation.surface: Someone shows keenness by arriving early and getting worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with keenness is doing it in an enthusiastic, impatient way, an adverb of manner.

clue.text: Not demanding land

definitions.meaning: a bird ... on a branch, meaning it lands or settles

explanation.surface: Undemanding territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb: to come down and settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy duties are called this, and an older verb meaning to alight or settle shares the spelling.

clue.text: Plinth under Eros? There you may find loud orator

indicators.note: There you may find tells you to look within the preceding words for the answer

explanation.surface: Beneath the statue of Eros in Piccadilly Circus you might find a soapbox speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros is the famous statue at Piccadilly Circus in London, a spot where street orators once held forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who thunders is a booming, forceful speaker; it was also the nickname of The Times newspaper.

clue.text: Sad rites recollected a calamity

indicators.note: recollected means collected again, i.e. regathered in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mournful ceremonies recalled a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered but means re-collected: shuffle SAD RITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sudden event causing great damage or suffering.

clue.text: Girl's father married

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies and forms

explanation.surface: A young woman's dad is a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short female first name, so a girl's name fits the definition.

clue.text: Former cleric keeping holy? The opposite

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds the other inside it
The opposite means swap the roles: the holy word keeps the cleric, not the other way round

parts.note: pious means devout or holy
Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a cleric

explanation.surface: A one-time priest holding on to sanctity, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, REV would hold PIOUS; 'The opposite' reverses that, so PIOUS holds REV: P(REV)IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives meaning earlier or preceding in time.

clue.text: Wound to make you give up

definitions.meaning: a wound, as from a knife
to give it up, as with smoking

explanation.surface: An injury that makes you quit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash in the skin is called this, and so is reducing or abandoning a habit, as in cutting out sugar.

clue.text: Veronica shows quickness — that is surprising!

parts.note: speed is quickness
Well! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A woman called Veronica proves surprisingly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name but is the botanical name for a plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the Latin genus name for the small blue-flowered plants also known by this common name.

clue.text: With this car you can see English country

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: From this vehicle you could view the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Type of vehicle: an estate is a car with an extended rear load area, a station wagon.

clue.text: More than one bird changes direction, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, and a different spelling with the same sound is entered

parts.note: turns means changes direction

explanation.surface: A flock of birds wheels in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: These are slender seabirds related to gulls; the plural fits 'more than one'.

clue.text: Ornate collar not properly ironed, you'd say?

indicators.note: you'd say means the word is spoken, and a different spelling with the same sound is entered

parts.note: rough means not smooth, as of cloth not properly ironed

explanation.surface: A fancy collar that has been badly pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stiff pleated frill worn round the neck in Elizabethan times, an elaborate neckpiece.

clue.text: After drink clique using speed

indicators.note: After means the clique word follows the drink word

parts.note: tea is a drink
a ring is a clique or gang

explanation.surface: After a drink, a gang goes off fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To go tearing along is to rush at great speed, a sense of the verb 'tear'.

clue.text: Everyone needs you initially for a friend

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of you

explanation.surface: Everybody needs you, first of all, as a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a supporter or associate on the same side.

clue.text: Most idiotic craze recalled before exam

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the exam word
recalled means called back, so the craze word is read backwards

parts.note: a fad is a craze
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A foolish fashion remembered before a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe the extreme of silliness; this is the superlative of a British word for foolish.

clue.text: Praises boys embracing university

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: lads are boys

explanation.surface: Students' lads are hugging their university.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: both mean commends or extols someone highly.
